title: Subadditivity of matrix rank over finite sums
statement:
Let $s$ be a finite subset of an index set, and let $(A_i)_{i \in s}$ be a family of real matrices with rows indexed by a set $X$ and columns indexed by a finite set $Y$. Then the rank of their sum is at most the sum of their ranks:
\[
  \mathrm{rank}\!\left(\sum_{i \in s} A_i\right) \;\le\; \sum_{i \in s} \mathrm{rank}(A_i).
\]
hypotheses_covered: family of real matrices A_i indexed by s
columns indexed by a finite set Y
replaced:
For any finite index set $\iota$, a finite set $s \subseteq \iota$, and a family
of matrices $A : \iota \to \mathbb{R}^{X \times Y}$,
\[
  \mathrm{rank}\!\left(\sum_{i \in s} A_i\right) \le \sum_{i \in s} \mathrm{rank}(A_i).
\]
